privacy.title: Your data
privacy.stored: For each checkup: the leaf photo (made smaller, with hidden camera data such as GPS removed), the diagnosis and advice, the heatmap, your answer to "Was this correct?", and who it belongs to: your account if you are signed in, otherwise a random ID for this browser. Your location only if you chose to share it.
privacy.public: Nothing that identifies you. The public map only shows how many disease reports came from an area of about 5 km², and only when at least 3 different browsers reported there. Your exact location, photos and checkups are never shown to anyone else.
privacy.location: Taken only after you agree: from your phone's location or, if that isn't available, from the location saved in the photo. You can stop sharing any time with "Change" on the Diagnose page. For the weather risk of potato and rice, a point rounded to about 5 km is sent to the free weather service Open-Meteo, with nothing that identifies you. For a PDF report, our server loads the map around that rounded area from OpenStreetMap.
privacy.delete: This removes every checkup made in this browser (or in your account, when you are signed in), with its photos, and every saved field, from our servers. It cannot be undone. A guest should do it before clearing the browser data: after that we can no longer tell which checkups and fields were theirs.
privacy.failed: Could not delete your data. Please try again.
privacy.fields: For each field you add for weather alerts: its crop, growth stage, an optional name and the place you chose, tied to your account, or to a random ID for this browser if you are a guest. The exact place is kept private: it is never shown, never in the public map and never in our logs. Only a point rounded to about 5 km is sent to the free weather service Open-Meteo, with nothing that identifies you. "Delete my data" removes your fields too, and each field also has its own Delete button under Profile and privacy.
privacy.contextTitle: Weather and soil for a checkup
privacy.context: The first time you open a checkup that has a location, our server looks up the weather around the photo date (Open-Meteo, the same point rounded to about 5 km), the rainfall compared with normal and a modelled soil map (through Google Earth Engine, which is sent only the centre of a square of about 250 m around your point, never the exact location). The result is saved with the checkup, without coordinates. Soil Health Card values you type in are saved with that checkup only. "Delete my data" removes all of it.
privacy.alertsTitle: Weather alerts: what leaves our server
privacy.alerts: The weather and the river forecast are asked for with a point rounded to about 5 km, never your field's exact place. Fires are asked for from NASA with the same rounded area (a box of about 22 km); the distance to a fire is worked out on our server. Official warnings (NDMA, IMD, the river gauges) news headlines and mandi prices are fetched by our server for everyone (for a state and a crop, never for a person), so nothing about you is sent for them. Saved fields stay until you delete them. Weather, river, fire and satellite answers are kept from half an hour to a few days and hold no personal data. The satellite flood check, which runs only when you press its button, is the one place where the exact point of your field goes to Google (Earth Engine): it reads a circle of 500 m around that point from public satellite images, and the answer is kept for 3 days under a code that does not show the place.
privacy.reportsTitle: Reports from other farmers, and your answers
privacy.reports: "Disease reports near you" uses the same data as the public disease map: a disease counts only when at least 3 different browsers reported it, your own browser is never counted, and the alert shows a disease and a number, never a place. "Did this help?" stores the rule, the date, your answer and the field's crop and growth stage, with no place; it is kept for a year, and "Delete my data" removes it.
privacy.accounts: Signing in is optional. If you create an account we store your name, your email and a scrambled (hashed) form of your password; we never see the password itself. Your checkups and fields then belong to the account instead of the browser, so they follow you to other phones. The sign-in is a token kept in this browser until you sign out, for at most 30 days (renewed each time you open the app); we use no cookies. You can delete the account, with everything in it, under Profile › My data.

mode.weatherSub: Rain, frost and heat for your fields

title.noFields: Add a field to get weather alerts.
title.unavailable: The weather could not be checked.
title.old: The last copy shows no alert, but it may be out of date.

FROST-WHEAT-1.head: Frost risk. Give a light irrigation in the evening before the cold night.
FROST-WHEAT-1.why: The forecast night low is {{value}} °C, and this level starts at {{threshold}} °C. Wheat that is flowering or filling grain is easily hurt by frost, and the ground can be colder than the forecast air.

FROST-POTATO-1.head: Frost risk. Irrigate lightly before the cold night, but not if heavy rain is forecast.
FROST-POTATO-1.why: The forecast night low is {{value}} °C, and this level starts at {{threshold}} °C. Frost burns potato leaves, and a light irrigation before the cold night is the usual protection.

HEAT-WHEAT-1.head: Hot weather for wheat. Give light, frequent irrigation in the evening and hold off fertiliser.
HEAT-WHEAT-1.why: The forecast daytime high is {{value}} °C, and this level starts at {{threshold}} °C. Heat at flowering and grain filling makes the crop age early and can lower the yield.

HEAT-RICE-1.head: Hot days while the rice flowers. Keep a thin layer of water in the field.
HEAT-RICE-1.why: The forecast daytime high is {{value}} °C, and this level starts at {{threshold}} °C. Above about 33 °C the pollen of flowering rice can fail, and then the grains do not fill.

HEAT-ANY-1.head: Very hot day ahead. Irrigate in the evening, protect people working outside and check the official IMD warning.
HEAT-ANY-1.why: The forecast daytime high is {{value}} °C, and this level starts at {{threshold}} °C, the heat wave level IMD uses for the plains. This is our own forecast check, not an official warning.

RAIN-HARVEST-1.head: Rain is coming before harvest is done. Cut the ripe crop first and keep it covered and dry.
RAIN-HARVEST-1.why: The forecast rain is {{value}} mm in one day, and this level starts at {{threshold}} mm. Rain on a ripe or cut crop causes grain loss and spoilage.

RAIN-HEAVY-1.head: Heavy rain expected. Open the field drains and put off spraying, fertiliser and irrigation.
RAIN-HEAVY-1.why: The forecast rain is {{value}} mm in one day, and this level starts at {{threshold}} mm. IMD calls 64.5 mm or more in a day heavy rain.

RAIN-SPRAY-1.head: Rain is coming. Hold off spraying, the rain will wash it off.
RAIN-SPRAY-1.why: The forecast rain is {{value}} mm in the next day or so, and this tip starts at {{threshold}} mm. A spray that is washed off is wasted and the leaf stays unprotected.

FLOOD-RIVER-1.head: River flow in your area is forecast to be unusually high {{day}}. Watch the water level, keep drains open and move tools and stored produce away from low ground.
FLOOD-RIVER-1.why: The forecast flow of the biggest river near your field reaches {{value}} m³/s, above {{threshold}} m³/s, a level it reaches on only a few days of the year. This is a forecast for the region with low confidence, not for your field: it does not mean your field will flood.

DRY-SPELL-1.head: Dry spell: {{value}} dry days in a row ({{day}}). Irrigate if you can: sowing, flowering and grain filling need moisture in the soil.
DRY-SPELL-1.why: A dry day is a day with less than 2.5 mm of rain. {{value}} in a row is past {{threshold}}, the level this alert starts at (IMD counts dry spells at 7 and 14 days). The forecast for one place can be wrong, so look at your soil too.

DRY-SPELL-2.head: Dry spell: {{value}} dry days in a row ({{day}}). Check the soil moisture, and irrigate if the crop is wilting.
DRY-SPELL-2.why: A dry day is a day with less than 2.5 mm of rain. {{value}} in a row is past {{threshold}}, the level this alert starts at for a young crop (IMD counts dry spells at 7 and 14 days). The forecast for one place can be wrong, so look at your soil too.

DISEASE-NEAR-1.head: Other farmers near you found {{disease}} on {{crop}} in the last {{window}} days. Look at your own plants soon.
DISEASE-NEAR-1.why: At least {{value}} different phones checked a {{crop}} leaf within about 5 km of this field and the AI read {{disease}}. These are photo checks by other users of this app, not lab results, and where each one was taken stays private. Compare with your own leaves.

FIRE-NEAR-1.head: A fire was seen by satellite within {{km}} km of your field in the last {{window}} hours. Check around your field now, and if smoke or flames come close, call 101.
FIRE-NEAR-1.why: NASA satellites saw {{count}} hot spots within 5 km of your field, the nearest within {{km}} km. A satellite passes only a few times a day and sees a fire only while it burns, so a small or short fire can be missed, and a hot spot is not always a crop fire. Our server works out the distance; NASA is only asked about the area around the field, not its exact place.

fire.caveat: A satellite sees a fire only when it passes, a few times a day. Not every hot spot is a crop fire, and no alert here does not mean there is no fire.
